question.problem: Find the mass of a cardboard object which has the form of a quarter-disk, in the second quadrant, of radius $4$ centered at the origin and mass density function $\lambda $ given by $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{2y}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}.$
question.worked_solution:
The mass of a quarter-disk $D$ of radius $4$ centered at the origin with mass density $\lambda (x,y)=\frac{2y}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ={∬}_{D}\frac{2y}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)\text{ }\text{d}A={∬}_{Δ}\text{ }\lambda (r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,r\text{ }drd\theta .
$$

First, let's sketch our region $D:$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14117153/assets/795390e471ee5e96892dfc979f96b803d4a9a4c267410a3afc60a6672f71e63d.png)

In polar coordinates $(r,\theta ),$ the region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ={(r,\theta )\,:\,0\le r\le 4,\,\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \pi }.
$$

Finally, using the change of variables formula, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\frac{2y}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{Δ}\frac{2(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )}{(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2}}\,r\,\text{d}r\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{4}2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta {\int }_{0}^{4}2\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta [2r]_{0}^{4}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta (8-0)\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =8{\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =8[-\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ]_{\pi /2}^{\pi } \\  & =8(-(-1)+0) \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the total mass of the quarter-disk is $M=8.$
